title: How Scale AI grew: narrow wedge, infinite markets, and hiring people who care
summary: Wang recounts how Scale started at YC as an API for human labor, won by focusing on self-driving data, then repeatedly built ahead of AI waves (OpenAI, defense, enterprise agents). He explains when to move from narrow markets to infinite ones, why specialized data and models will be a company's IP, and why caring deeply is the trait he hires for.

principles.text: If an incumbent product is widely mentioned but awful in practice, that's a good sign there's room to win.
principles.quote: whenever you're in a space and that's kind of the like that's like the thing. It's like people mention a thing, but it sucks, that's usually like a pretty good sign.

principles.text: Focus on one seemingly narrow, fast-growing vertical to build momentum quickly, even if it can't sustain the final business.
principles.quote: it is both true that it enabled us to build the business to be to get to scale pretty very quickly and it is also true that that was not a big enough market to sustain a gigantic business.

principles.text: Start in the narrowest market, then switch gears toward infinite markets if you want a $100B company.
principles.quote: early on you're trying to go for very very narrow markets like almost the narrowest markets you can and then you're just trying to like gain momentum and then sort of like slowly grow out from those hyper narrow markets

principles.text: Serve the layer every wave of a technology depends on, so you end up building ahead of the trend.
principles.quote: for AI to be successful in any vertical area it needed data and so like our demand for our our products would preede a lot of times the actual sort of like evolution of AI into those industries.

principles.text: Differentiation comes from encoding your unique business problems into data and environments for specialized models.
principles.quote: alpha in the modern world will be determined by you know to what degree you're able to sort of like encapsulate your business problems into data sets or environments

principles.text: Hire people who deeply care about their work; the magnitude of care is the strongest signal of success.
principles.quote: I wrote this post many years ago called hire people who give a and it really is pretty simple.
